description: Deterministic CrossTL/CrossGL shared feature spec extracted from the committed CrossTL frontend snapshot and cross-repo language contract manifest. It is a tooling/spec contract artifact only.

feature_groups.description: Branching, loops, scoped declarations, early returns, and statement AST forms shared by both frontends.
Representative CrossTL example programs plus legal language forms that may remain target/backend unsupported.
Descriptor arrays, symbolic/folded/dynamic descriptor indexes, nonuniform markers, and runtime array boundary cases.
Arithmetic/comparison operators, casts, constructors, swizzles, loads/stores, and scalar/vector intrinsic calls.
Shader modules, graphics/compute stage blocks, and named compute entry points accepted by the v0 frontend surface.
Layout metadata, descriptor resources, storage buffers/images, access qualifiers, and resource arrays.
Texture/sampler/image resource types, shadow compare forms, LOD/manual compare helpers, and texture/image intrinsics.
Primitive/vector/matrix/named types, structs, constants, and fixed/runtime array forms.

negative_cases.reason: A v0 shader must declare at least one compilable stage.
A v0 stage block must contain an explicit entry function.
break is only legal inside loop constructs.
Duplicate cbuffer member names are ambiguous in unqualified references.
CrossTL accepts extended stages such as geometry, but native compiler v0 only lowers vertex, fragment, and compute stages.
CrossTL accepts ray any-hit stage blocks, but native compiler v0 only lowers vertex, fragment, and compute stages.
CrossTL accepts ray callable stage blocks, but native compiler v0 only lowers vertex, fragment, and compute stages.
CrossTL accepts ray closest-hit stage blocks, but native compiler v0 only lowers vertex, fragment, and compute stages.
CrossTL accepts ray generation stage blocks, but native compiler v0 only lowers vertex, fragment, and compute stages.
CrossTL accepts ray intersection stage blocks, but native compiler v0 only lowers vertex, fragment, and compute stages.
CrossTL accepts ray miss stage blocks, but native compiler v0 only lowers vertex, fragment, and compute stages.
CrossTL accepts tessellation stage blocks, but native compiler v0 only lowers vertex, fragment, and compute stages.

CrossTL accepts colon-style variable declarations; native compiler v0 accepts function-body colon-style locals and bare uninitialized stage-scope shared value declarations, but still rejects initialized stage-scope var colon declarations.
CrossTL accepts generic declarations, but native compiler v0 has no generic specialization or monomorphization path.
CrossTL accepts impl declarations, but native compiler v0 has no trait or impl lowering contract.
CrossTL accepts source import declarations, but native compiler v0 does not resolve source imports.
CrossTL accepts physical line-splicing tolerance before preprocessor/importer tokenization, but native compiler v0 does not promise backslash-newline splicing as shared .cgl syntax.
CrossTL accepts match/pattern control forms, but native compiler v0 does not lower them.
CrossTL accepts switch/case/default statements, but native compiler v0 only lowers restricted non-fallthrough scalar switch forms.
CrossTL accepts duplicate switch case labels, but native compiler v0 rejects duplicate folded scalar labels to avoid silently shadowing later cases.
CrossTL accepts grouped switch case labels, but native compiler v0 requires each case section to have its own terminal break-delimited body.
CrossTL accepts switch case labels with expressions of different scalar types, but native compiler v0 requires labels compatible with the selector type.
CrossTL accepts break statements inside switch sections, but native compiler v0 only strips a terminal switch-local break from each case body.
CrossTL accepts for-in loop statements, but native compiler v0 only lowers C-style for loops.
CrossTL accepts this incomplete for header shape, but native compiler v0 requires the accepted fixture's C-style init, condition, and update header form.
CrossTL accepts preprocessor nodes, but native compiler v0 does not run or preserve a source preprocessor.
CrossTL accepts trait declarations, but native compiler v0 has no trait or impl lowering contract.
CrossTL accepts broader var address-space declarations, but native compiler v0 only accepts workgroup/shared stage-scope var storage.
